html:
Wineport (A16)

Region in the English rating survey: Wescann / Gerudia.

In one sentence: Turn wine-producing cities that escaped their lords into a league with armies, overseas vineyards and global markets.

Story: high | Mission-tree length: long (61 direct mission definitions, including conditional continuations) | Mission-tree currency: the local installation contains the reworked tree | Distinctiveness: high | Tedium: medium | Early pressure: medium-high | Expansion capacity: above average. Both base Mod and localisation support EU4 v1.37.5.0; the old 2021 dev diary cannot override the reworked rules.

Identity and history

Wineport is a Regent Court merchant republic in Lencenor's Bay of Wines. The name denotes both the city and the League of Winebay's country Tag in the game. “Forming the League of Winebay” therefore does not mean there was no league before 1419. [Local history; localisation]

The opening primer starts the story in 1419. During the Third Lilac War, the Duke of Íselsuin died without an heir and his duchy collapsed. Wineport, Foxalley, Coruan and Bottlepoint signed a covenant amid the disorder, seeking independence and prosperity through good wine. Rubenaire seized Coruan during the chaos, leaving an unresolved grievance. [Local flavour text]

During the Fourth Lilac War, the league stayed neutral, accepted Toarnaire's suzerainty from the Moon Party and supplied mercenaries to both sides, accumulating wealth. In 1444 the league, led by Énri the Taster, faces a resurgent Lorent and surrounding Winelords. First defend independence, then fulfil the covenant's ambition to become Lencenor's greatest wine producer and trader. The Chinese research flagged an incomplete ruler-name encoding; the current history's raw bytes decode as Énri in CP1252, and the English opening primer independently confirms that spelling. No speculative name reconstruction is needed. [Local history; flavour text; localisation]

National story and campaign arc

This is not a country that sits in one port waiting for income to rise. Early on, reorder Winebay politics and restore the city league, turning merchants' wealth into dependable defence. Mercenary organisation and shipbuilding let a trading republic defend independence without removing pressure from Lorent and neighbouring Winelords. [Local flavour text]

In midgame the story expands from local vintners into a cross-regional production and sales network. Manage wine country, overseas vineyards and trade routes, deal with lizardfolk cities and enlarge both supplies and markets. Its distinguishing feature is sustained attention to one commodity: urban politics, agricultural investment and overseas enterprise affect one another through wine.

Eventually choose an institutional direction: continue the republic and league project, strengthening its identity while changing the name, ideas and later missions; or adopt Winelord monarchy and make commercial strength a basis for dynastic rivalry. A free republican league and Lorent's crown are not unconditional cumulative endpoints. [Local events]

Core mechanics

First is the wine industry's mission loop. Some nodes require cash reserves, production development, production buildings and manufactories. Reinvest income in the supply chain rather than spending everything on more troops. “The Winetide” requires 1000 in the treasury and explicitly executes add_treasury = -1000 on completion. It also selects two qualifying Escanni wine provinces for production increases and upgrades the wine modifier. This node spends money rather than merely checking the balance. [Local script]

Second is converting overseas production. “Forests of Bloodwine” requires control of 15 provinces and at least 5 meeting production-development prerequisites, then converts five qualifying provinces to wine and applies long-term benefits. “Blood” in the title is not proof of slavery: the reviewed effects concern land control, production and trade-good conversion. [Local script]

Third is wine events and market relations. The rework adds a wine-collection narrative. A lizard-market event offers spending 500 to improve lizardfolk tolerance, or lowering tolerance instead. Mission prose also proposes installing cooperative regimes to secure trade. This is not an entirely gentle pastoral republic, but the reviewed material does not establish a lizardfolk slave industry. [Local events; flavour text]

Fourth is upgrading the league's identity. A same-Tag renaming event changes the country's colour, ideas and mission route and takes it out of the Empire. This reorganises institutions and objectives within A16; it does not create a new league Tag. [Local script]

Play by phase and endgame

First secure independence, finances and relations with neighbours, then invest in Winebay production and defence. Do not assume the imperial protection recommended in old guides survives the later league route. In midgame coordinate wine provinces, production buildings, the navy and colonial trade. Expanding too broadly too early makes investment and warfare compete for the same funds.

Upgrading the league late keeps A16, sets a new-ideas flag, replaces non-generic missions and closes the Lorent formation route. The other event option changes to monarchy and the Winelord reform. An eligible Lencori country without the league flag can, under the other general conditions, form Lorent A01, change Tag and switch trees. This is an optional detour, not the republic's inevitable ending. [Local decisions; events]

61 is the current index's count of direct definitions. Same-Tag upgrading replaces missions; it does not guarantee that every mission stays visible simultaneously from opening to endgame.

Personality and recommendations

The v2.1 coordinates are expansion 64/100 | autocracy 30/100 | magic–artifice direction 50/100 (100 = magic, 0 = artifice; theme intensity 18/100) | pluralism 60/100. Alternative profiles distinguish the merchant republic and league (autocracy 30) from the optional Winelord monarchy detour (autocracy 75), not a compulsory transition between them.

Its v2.1 values classification is Neutral (64/100), with a branch-dependent trajectory. The v2.1 coordinates—expansion 64, autocracy 30, magic direction 50 (intensity 18) and pluralism 60—describe a merchant league first. Warfare and colonisation serve production and markets; choosing Winelord monarchy has a separate autocracy coordinate of 75. The middle magic-direction coordinate is only descriptive at this low intensity and should not dominate matching.

The values assessment is Neutral 64, with a branch-dependent trajectory: dignity 65, public good 78, personhood 60 and restraint 45. City independence, industrial construction and the option to welcome lizardfolk merchants support the positive side. Installing cooperative regimes for market interests shows disregard for foreign autonomy. The existing evidence does not establish that bloodwine production itself enslaves residents, and colonisation, warfare or adopting monarchy do not automatically lower the score. Overall confidence remains medium; merchant-republic status is no guarantee of goodness.

Recommended for players who enjoy trade, agricultural investment, a commodity theme, navies and moderate colonisation. Avoid it if you dislike production chains, want only land-army conquest or insist on imperial protection throughout the campaign.

Community experience and evidence boundaries

Official Dev Diary #17 presents the early design; #85 introduces the 2025 rework. Their version contexts remain separate. Player discussions dated 2024-05-04 and 2024-10-30 praise income and high-development play while discussing imperial protection, colonisation and Lorent's pressure. Both predate the rework; the second also discusses the Winescales submod, which is excluded from base-Mod mechanics. [Official development diaries; community opinion]

The Wiki confirms the city's trading role but does not supply an adequate foundation chronology; the 1419 background comes from the current opening text. No historical-map original was obtained. See the original evidence page for sources, route exclusions and the older-post boundary. The English source-text receipt records the newly noticed treasury and encoding discrepancies without changing the Chinese research or scores.

National Ideas

The following reproduces the current local national-idea text and script effects. Traditions apply when the set is adopted; the seven ideas unlock in sequence as points are invested, and the ambition applies after all seven are unlocked. Only national ideas are listed: racial, government and mission bonuses are excluded. A successor idea set does not automatically stack with the earlier set. Idea descriptions may recall history or express future aspirations; they do not automatically establish events already completed in 1444. Names and complete descriptions use the current Mod’s English localisation. Alternative and predecessor/successor sets remain separately conditional, including whether new ideas are accepted on formation.

Effect display units inherited from the source data are reproduced for parity, not revalidated here. Suspicious percentages and script-valued effects require separate review; raw values are shown below.

Wineport (A16) — Wineporter Ideas

Set ID: A16_ideas. Source: project-verified Mod script (public artifact omits local path and line offsets).

Applicability condition (source script):

    trigger = {
        tag = A16 #Wineport
        NOT = { has_country_flag = wineport_upgraded_ideas }
    }

Wineporter Traditions

  • Domestic trade power: +10% (global_own_trade_power; raw value 0.1).

  • Ship trade power: +25% (global_ship_trade_power; raw value 0.25).

1. Winebay Shipwrights

The Winebay was always destined to be a center of naval infrastructure, boasting shallow water, warm climate and nearby forests. This opportune location attracted the attention of the Damerian Republic, which quickly sent settlers to the region to found urban centers along the bay. With them came the Damerian shipbuilding tradition.

Among these urban centers, one quickly overshadowed the other in terms of importance: Wineport. The city at the mouth of Bloodwine connected Lencenor to the rest of the Divenhal and as such became a center of trade rivaling Damucen and Damescrown. The fortune brought by trade was reinvested to expand the shipyards and harbor, allowing the city to maintain and amplify its shipbuilding knowledge.

The ships built in Wineport have seen many battles across the centuries: they helped Dameria rule the sea, battled the fleet of the Black Castanor and smashed through the Imperial fleet during the Lilac Wars. Even in defeat, they always prove their quality.

  • Naval combat bonus off owned coasts: +1 (own_coast_naval_combat_bonus; raw value 1.0).

2. Council of Seventy Chalices

When the League of Winebay was established, the great nobles of Lorent lost influence in the region, allowing many families, mainly lower nobles and merchants to fill the void. Often referred to as Wine Barons, for their role in the local production and trade of wine, these families formed the Seventy Chalices, an advisory body with great sway over the politics of the League. The Chalices gather once a month; after the ritual sharing of a cup of wine from one of the seventy vineyards of the region, the Chalices and leaders of the League discuss the direction of Winebay’s politics.

As a show of faith, and to further cooperation with the ruling body of the League, the Chalices have offered their private armies and fortified vineyards to the protection of Wineport and the surrounding city. A small price to pay to ensure their interests are taken care of.

  • Mercenary Discipline: +5% (mercenary_discipline; raw value 0.05).

  • Fort defense: +10% (defensiveness; raw value 0.1).

3. Wineport Cheeks

Most distinct among all traits of the Wineporter is their disposition. Be it their ruling elites with their reputation for joviality , or their merchants - said to never be trustworthy without a couple of drinks - the Wineporter lives a joyful life, a large smile on their flushed faces and the pleasant alcoholic sting of Milk of Minara, Madalairey White or Eilísin Tríros on their tongue.

“To have Wineport cheeks” has thus come to describe anyone living a carefree and easy life. And while other Lorentish may disapprove of the reputation of wine obsession this gives them, the Wineporters rejoice to be known for their festive lives.

  • National unrest: -2 (global_unrest; raw value -2).

4. Urban Centers of Lencenor

When Dameria founded cities along the Winebay, Wineport was built as a trading outpost at the mouth of the Bloodwine River. Good relations with the local Cingeti and the neighboring Sormanni led to many of them joining the Damerian settlers, transforming the outpost into the largest city of Lencenor and an important center of trade for the republic. When Dameria burned during the Dragonwake in 474, Wineport suffered from the loss of trade and the many wars that devastated the region. It wasn’t until the Peace of Lorenan in 529 that the city recovered and saw new extensions being built, but by that point it had lost relevance to Lorentei. When the elves arrived during the war of the Sorcerer-King, Wineport greatly expanded as many elves settled the city, their expertise greatly appreciated in the many shipyards of the city. As a result of this large elven population and its western position, Wineport became the main port visited by the Sea Elves.

  • Development cost: -5% (development_cost; raw value -0.05).

  • Production efficiency: +5% (production_efficiency; raw value 0.05).

5. The Bloodwine Oath

“By the Blood of the River, I swear to serve, with honor and fidelity…”

Part of the Bloodwine Oath

The soldiers and marines of Wineport swear an oath, commonly known as the Rubenairey Oath, after the river the city is built upon. They would wear uniforms made of expensive Redglades fabrics in the color of Rubenaire Red and Saloren Blue. The merchants adopted both the oath as a show of loyalty and the colors, often worn on cavalier cloaks. To this day the oath can be found in the motto of the city and the color is a staple of Wineporter fashion.

  • Marine force limit: +25% (allowed_marine_fraction; raw value 0.25).

6. Adherents of the Whiterose Court

Spreading from Lorentainé to the shore of Deranne, the Whiterose Court was a variation of the Regent Court present in Northern Lencenor before the centralisation of the Court. Born from the merging of the Lencori worship of Adean and Minara, the Whiterose promoted knightly ideals, joy and celebrations.

While Wineport mainly followed the tenets of the House of Minara, during the Ioriellan empire, the Whiterose Court expanded to the city, principally to its merchant elites. Even if the Wineporter continued to indulge themself as expected of followers of Minara, many adopted adeanic tradition under the influence of the Whiterose. Knight-Burghers emerged from the merchants of Wineport and the Vinterscourt, the main adeanic temple in the Winebay before Minara’s rise, was restored to its previous glory.

With the revelation of the death of Castellos in 1518, the Whiterose Court experienced a resurgence. Its beliefs bled into and merged with those of those of the Court, as Adean ascended to his rightful throne and the Lencori rose with him.

  • Diplomatic reputation: +100% (diplomatic_reputation; raw value 1).

7. WFTC

Founded in the sixteenth century by the Wine Baron Awen Redriver, the Winebay Foreign Trading Company is the largest trading company in Lorent. It owes its success to its cooperation with Lorentish colonial structures, which allowed it to quickly spread its influence to the colonies in Aelantir, the outposts of Sarhal and even the distant lands of Haless and Insyaa.

The company boasts a large merchant navy; the red and blue sails of its ships can be found in every major port of the world, be it Brasan, Anbenncóst, Isobelin or Tianlou. From there and many more places, they return to Wineport with holds full of foreign goods. While Lorentainé remains the capital of Lorent, in the mind of many Wineport is its beating heart, connecting the mainland to its overseas possessions, thanks in part to the effort of the WFTC.

  • Number of merchants: +1 (merchants; raw value 1).

  • Naval Force Limit Modifier: +10% (naval_forcelimit_modifier; raw value 0.1).

Wineporter Ambition

  • Ship trade power propagation: +20% (ship_power_propagation; raw value 0.2).

Wineport (A16) — Winebayer Ideas

Set ID: A16_upgrade_ideas. Source: project-verified Mod script (public artifact omits local path and line offsets).

Applicability condition (source script):

    trigger = {
        tag = A16 #Wineport
        has_country_flag = wineport_upgraded_ideas
    }

Winebayer Traditions

  • Naval Morale: +10% (naval_morale; raw value 0.10).

  • Ship trade power: +25% (global_ship_trade_power; raw value 0.25).

1. Winebay Shipwrights

The Winebay was always destined to be a center of naval infrastructure, boasting shallow water, warm climate and nearby forests. This opportune location attracted the attention of the Damerian Republic, which quickly sent settlers to the region to found urban centers along the bay. With them came the Damerian shipbuilding tradition.

Among these urban centers, one quickly overshadowed the other in terms of importance: Wineport. The city at the mouth of Bloodwine connected Lencenor to the rest of the Divenhal and as such became a center of trade rivaling Damucen and Damescrown. The fortune brought by trade was reinvested to expand the shipyards and harbor, allowing the city to maintain and amplify its shipbuilding knowledge.

The ships built in Wineport have seen many battles across the centuries: they helped Dameria rule the sea, battled the fleet of the Black Castanor and smashed through the Imperial fleet during the Lilac Wars. Even in defeat, they always prove their quality.

  • Naval combat bonus off owned coasts: +1 (own_coast_naval_combat_bonus; raw value 1).

2. Vanguard of the Seventy Chalices

Our rise to power would not be possible without the help and support of the Wine Barons. Their organisation, the Council of Seventy Chalices, was instrumental in providing both advice and mercenaries to the League. Their acumen for trade and wealth, combined with their deep coffers to hire skilled mercenaries, has meant that we have shared many a glass with the Barons of the Seventy Chalices to their help and our success.

But a glass shared amongst friends is little reward for the service they have rendered, and so our League has elevated the Seventy Chalices to an official organ of state. This privileged position has only made us firmer allies, and their fortified vineyards now serve as bulwarks of the League, ready to face off against any opponent who we now share. The Vanguard of the Seventy Chalices, as their mercenaries are now nicknamed, fight alongside state troops to further our goals of gold and good wine.

  • Mercenary Discipline: +5% (mercenary_discipline; raw value 0.05).

  • Fort defense: +20% (defensiveness; raw value 0.20).

3. Drunk like a Winebayer

A traditional stereotype of a Winebayer says that when a Winebayer isn’t working, they are drinking, and even when they are working, they’re looking for an opportunity to take a break and drink. In fact, many travellers say that Wineporters spend every day drunk, and that we are simply so acclimatised to drinking we barely notice it.

While rather an exaggeration, there is a kernel of truth in these descriptions, as any Winebayer knows they can easily outdrink other Lencori. When they are sliding off their chairs, we are politely asking the waiter for another glass. This often becomes an aid in wars, where the heavy drinking culture of our soldiers keeps spirits high without an impact on their fighting prowess. They simply discharge their volleys and charge into melee with red cheeks and a smile, with no less discipline than their sober opponents.

  • Army morale: +15% (land_morale; raw value 0.15).

4. Lencori Urban Enlightment

Where once humble trading towns stood, great cities arise. Where once empty land, unused, stood, towns, guilds, manufacturers and warehouses have taken their place. And where once humble merchants plied their wares locally, international traders import and export luxury goods on a grand scale. Under our oversight, these achievements have all been made a reality as the cities of the League have grown and expanded with our power and wealth.

As the League continues its expansion into new markets and the influence of our goods spread further, this will only help to develop the cities under our control. The barrels of wine will keep on rolling through their streets, downhill to the ports, and from those ports shall wealth flow back up to the manors of our barons.

  • Production efficiency: +10% (production_efficiency; raw value 0.10).

5. The Bloodwine Loyals

‘...Under my watch shall Wineport be safe. I will protect it from all who seek to harm it, be they mundane or monstrous. By my hand, shall the happiness and wealth of its citizens be safe…’ Part of the Bloodwine Oath

The Rubenairey Oath has become the ultimate symbol of the both the strength and loyalty of Wineport, and the Leage of Winebay as a whole. All those sailors and marines who have bled in our cause have done so under the words of the oath, and without their sacrifice, the citizens of the Winebay recognise our prosperous position would never have been possible.

This has led to the Oath taking on an almost mythical role, and its devotees - marines, sailors, and those who are devoted to our goals - swear to uphold its every word and command, and provide their lives to the League and its safety.

  • Marine force limit: +30% (allowed_marine_fraction; raw value 0.30).

6. Whiterose Circles

It has been noted by many of our traders that it appears the rest of Cannor is tearing themselves apart over religion. Whether it is the firebrands proclaiming Corin as the successor to Castellos, or the Ravelians saying there is only one God, they have brought out their swords, firearms and spells to decide which faith is the most righteous. We look at all of this with… disappointment. But, then again, we cannot expect all to be as sensible as us, as we stay true to Adean and Minara.

It is they who we must look to in this time of trouble - Adean to answer to the challenges of the other faiths, and Minara to bring joy in such troubled times. Though they may try to influence our thoughts and our beliefs, the Whiterose court and Adeanism shall remain steadfast in the Winebay!

  • True faith tolerance: +2 (tolerance_own; raw value 2).

7. WCCC

The Winebay Foreign Trading Company has grown alongside our own state. As more of Halann has been mapped and charted, the WFTC has not been far behind these pioneers. Their ship holds are laden with barrels of wine, ready to trade it for the exotic goods that places such as Aelantir, Sarhal and Haless have to offer. And with every major port they stop at, another WFTC trading post is created, spreading our influence of the League across the globe.

The WFTC, owing to its recent success, has undergone a rebrand, and is now called the Winebay Company of Colonisation and Commerce, or W3C for short. It now places its ambitions higher, just like our League - Not only shall we sell the world wine, we shall expand our own tastes, and all their wine shall come to us! Whether that is through bargaining or more direct colonial measures shall be up for us and the W3C to decide.

  • Number of merchants: +1 (merchants; raw value 1).

  • Naval Force Limit Modifier: +20% (naval_forcelimit_modifier; raw value 0.20).

Winebayer Ambition

  • Ship Cost: -10% (global_ship_cost; raw value -0.10).

Lorent (A01) — Lorentish Ideas

Set ID: A01_ideas. Source: project-verified Mod script (public artifact omits local path and line offsets).

Applicability condition (source script):

    trigger = {
        tag = A01
    }

Lorentish Traditions

  • Cavalry combat ability: +20% (cavalry_power; raw value 0.2).

  • Diplomatic relations: +1 (diplomatic_upkeep; raw value 1).

1. Scions of Lorenan

Lorenan the Great was a charismatic Lencori chieftain and hero who united all Lencenor with the aid of the Ruby Dwarves. His realm split asunder after his passing. Now Lorent stands as this great realm restored, reborn and reunited, but for the squabbles of insurgent Winelords. Centuries of sibling rivalry and interregnum ended with the Rewantis dynasty victorious against the rival legacies of the Rubentis, Caylentis and Dameris. They gave way to the Siloriel name in turn, during the reforging of the realm that the War of the Sorcerer-King wrought.

Just as Lorenan had his personal companions, Lorent has her knights, the envy of Cannor. The different cavalry traditions of the different Lencori tribes are embodied in their modern prowess. Their plumage and formations inspiring renewed pride amidst even the smoke of battlefields in the modern era. A Lorentish regiment may be temporarily confused amidst the fray, but theirs is a cavalry that still concludes the carnage of war.

  • Army morale: +10% (land_morale; raw value 0.1).

2. Ioriellan Court Code

Ioriel Redrose, progenitor of the Siloriel family named after her, brought Lorent’s court to a new height during the times of the Iorellan Empire. Under her wise counsel, Lorentish diplomatic customs came to extend throughout much of Cannor.

An orphan on the Remnant Fleet, she prioritised patience in her life as her way of soothing differences and accumulating power. The court code she advocated for brought with it a sense of propriety in patience, slowing down courtly life. These ideas of deliberation as virtuous in and of itself aided the soft power of highly-elvenised Lorent, the proclivities of elves and half-elves enabling them to be the paragons of this code. The blossom of these ideals an entrenchment of the new aristocratic generation that remade Cannor in the wake of the War of the Sorcerer-King’s end in 1022.

Even now, Lorentish etiquette and court standards are praised and valued all across Cannor. The Siloriel have good claim to be the greatest Silver Family, especially compared to the mixed fortunes of the Silmuna. Theirs is the language of Cannorian diplomacy; theirs is the culture of prestige; and theirs are the instruments of many a treaty.

  • Diplomatic reputation: +200% (diplomatic_reputation; raw value 2).

  • Diplomatic annexation cost: -10% (diplomatic_annexation_cost; raw value -0.1).

3. Ruling Queens of Lorent

The Lencori avoided the imposition of patriarchal norms that afflicted those stomped underneath Castanor’s boot thanks to maintaining their independence. Wherein Ioriel came, she alongside general elven influences cemented this tradition twofold; when it might otherwise have been eroded with time and Cannorian norms being unified.

So it is that Lorentish queens rule with full power and women of noble stature are encouraged to join the high councils, with equal inheritance as the law of the Lorentish lands ensuring the full benefit of women’s voices. It is no shock that Minara’s influence is felt here with her sovereign temple’s presence upholding this tradition.

  • Female advisor chance: +40% (female_advisor_chance; raw value 0.4).

  • Governing Capacity Modifier: +15% (governing_capacity_modifier; raw value 0.15).

4. The Voyages of Endral

Endral was an elf from the Gladegate who rediscovered Aelantir in the name of the Ruby Crown in the year 1490. He was said to always be in search of the next horizon, at home in Lencenor, but always wondering that if one home was good, why not chart the way back to Aelantir and claim another! Praised after his return and mapper of the coasts and islands of the Ruined Sea in his famed three voyages, he was ennobled as Duke of Endralliande for his merit for his efforts spearheaded the Lorentish colonization of Aelantir for the next century. His first two voyages mapped out both sides of Endralliande and his final voyage took him past Soruin as he continued his journeys to see what had become of the ancient homeland.

He put his name on his discoveries and this first colony became the most developed of Lorent, as people moved into the strangely deserted land in search of new homes and to see what became of the ancient genesis of the elves. One of the original vessels of his fleet was even preserved as a museum ship in the colonial capital of Endralliande, a reminder of how much Lorentish shipbuilding and its empire owed to Elven innovations and individuals who worked with their human counterparts as part of this inheritance that was core to the whole national myth of Lorent.

  • Colonists: +1 (colonists; raw value 1).

  • Global trade power: +10% (global_trade_power; raw value 0.1).

5. First and Last Spear

When many other Cannorian realms abandoned Adean in the Crimson Deluge’s wake, the Lorentish remained true for he had seemingly protected them from Corin’s wroth. Lencenor was spared from the devastation and that was taken as divine provenance for their fealty to the leal successor among divinity just as they emulated his gallant ideal on Halann.

The Whiterose Court sect of the Regent Court started here, and its Renaissance bloom became a temporal lance for Adean on Halann, with a Counter-Reformation from beneath his renewed aegis. Even as Ravelianism arose, Lorent weathered that storm in kind, all but alone in their faith. Their faith in Castellos’ rightful successor asks no question, their devotion passing any earthly test. The Lorentish weathered the wars of religion within and without.

  • True faith tolerance: +2 (tolerance_own; raw value 2).

  • Manpower from true faith provinces: +20% (manpower_in_true_faith_provinces; raw value 0.20).

6. The Rose Fleet

The heart of Lorent’s colonial power rests upon its great fleet, built from Endral’s foundations to defend Lorentish interests in Aelantir and beyond and with patronage from Reánna V. During her short twelve year reign the court even moved to Westport as part of this focus on the bounty of the ocean and mercantile elites, before returning to Lorentaine under her successors with the aristocracy’s primacy restored anew.

Expert sailors, noble captains and the drydocks at Oldport and Westport ensure the domination of the Lament and the safety of our trade as our reach extends across the Globe and the goods of every nation find their way to Lorentish shores. These goods put Lorentish society at the forefront of every artistic movement and culinary trend as its navy ensured those goods always safely made their way to the growing colonial ports first and foremost.

The Rose Fleet proved itself the envy of the world during the 1600s campaign to end Aelnar. Its maintenance of supremacy at sea enabled the atrocities to be put to an end. Ensuring new Lorentish colonies were established in former Star Elven domains. It’s history of success at home in Cannor and at seas in the colonies, she is the envy of lesser nations with a naval lineage as pristine as the aristocrats in her captaincy.

  • Heavy ship combat ability: +10% (heavy_ship_power; raw value 0.1).

7. Petals of the Flower

Only Lorent, in the modern history of Halann, has been able to make every inhabited continent fear the same military force of well drilled, marked by their distinctive rose uniforms. As dominion expanded, the lessons of fighting in Aelantir were brought to Sarhal, from Sarhal to Haless as the might of Lorentish force of arms went from strength to strength. The Lorentish empire was not won by accident and these uniforms proved it, everywhere they went.

The modern Lorentish army arose out of the reorganisation of the realm following the Lorentish Wars of Religion. Highlighting the danger of divided forces with their own armies at the centre of the metropole. And, more crucially; of the need for an army directly loyal to this burgeoning state. Especially as her peers began to put their own houses in order, one after another. The Camiran Empire of Anbennar, the Small Country’s war of independence and the rise of the Northern League all showed how fragile the order in Cannor could be.

How close to home the danger could be; allowing for new taxes to be levied, standards to be set and new systems of recruitment to be put in place. These would secure a parity at home, putting Lorent in a strong position to expand as far as Rahen in time.

  • Discipline: +5% (discipline; raw value 0.05).

Lorentish Ambition

  • Vassal force limit contribution: +100% (vassal_forcelimit_bonus; raw value 1.0).
